fact: 1911年12月12日，德里觐见大典（Delhi Durbar）在城北的加冕公园举行，乔治五世与玛丽王后亲临，这是英国在位君主首次踏上印度土地。到场者包括约600名土邦王公、2万名士兵与大量官员，观礼人数在10万至20万之间，入场时鸣101响礼炮。大典前后，另有数十万人赶到红堡，从窗户观看国王夫妇。

sources.title: 100 years ago: A one million pound announcement（Rediff News，2011-12-13）
sources.quote: It cost the British government in India upwards of a million pounds and took a long year of preparations. It marked the coronation of George V and was the very first visit of a British monarch to Indian soil ... When George V ... arrived at the Durbar at noon on that chilly day in December a 101-gun salute was fired. Some 200,000 people, Indians and Britishers, were expected to attend the Durbar. And another half million people journeyed to the Red Fort for a darshan with the royal couple

sources.title: CORONATION PARK（The Delhi Monument Project）
sources.quote: The Durbar was held on 12 December 1911, and was the greatest spectacle of the British Raj: nearly 100,000 spectators gathered as the King – who, for the first time, attended in person – made two announcements that changed the course of Indian history

fact: 在1911年12月12日的觐见大典上，乔治五世宣布两件事：把英属印度政府所在地从加尔各答迁往德里，以及撤销1905年对孟加拉的分治、重新合并东孟加拉与西孟加拉。12月15日，国王夫妇在加冕公园场地为将于德里西南新建的都城奠基；该城后来由勒琴斯与贝克设计，1931年落成。

sources.title: CORONATION PARK（The Delhi Monument Project）
sources.quote: nearly 100,000 spectators gathered as the King – who, for the first time, attended in person – made two announcements that changed the course of Indian history: proclaiming the reunion of east and west Bengal (which had been partitioned in 1905 much to popular uproar), and transferring the capital from Calcutta to a newly built city in Delhi ... The foundation stones of the new city were laid, and it would become New Delhi.

sources.title: New Delhi（Wikipedia，引 1911 Durbar 记录）
sources.quote: The foundation stone of New Delhi was laid by King George V and Queen Mary at the site of Delhi Durbar of 1911 at Kingsway Camp on 15 December 1911, during their imperial visit.

fact: 大典的花费在不同记载中为90万至100万英镑以上。其中一说是英国政府批准60万英镑用于大典及接待到访的土邦统治者，印度政府另出30万英镑支付参加阅兵与警戒的8万名军队；筹备期长达一年，在加冕公园一带搭起临时城市，电力与供水从零铺设。

sources.title: Coronation Park, Delhi（Alchetron，汇总 Durbar 记录）
sources.quote: In 1911, a fabulous sum of Stg £600,000 was approved for the Durbar and maintenance of the visiting local rulers. An additional £300,000 were supplied by the Government of India to pay for eighty thousand Army troops in the parades and security for the event.

sources.title: CORONATION PARK（The Delhi Monument Project）
sources.quote: Preparations started a year in advance, with an elaborate temporary city being built – a sprawling area of about 200 square kilometres. Infrastructure like electricity and water was built from scratch, and the total cost of the Durbar was 900,000 pounds.

fact: 新德里的工地上，承包商从拉贾斯坦雇用了约6000名Bagadi（巴加迪）石工与土工，石材从多尔普尔运来；男工日薪约80派萨，女工日薪约60派萨。同一材料记载，承包商索巴·辛格在康诺特广场一带以每平方码2卢比的自由保有价购入地块。

sources.title: Sobha Singh (builder)（中文维基镜像，转译英文维基条目）
sources.quote: 他從拉賈斯坦邦僱用了約6,000名Bagadi勞動者,並從Dholpur進口的Stone僱用了數十名主管,文員和會計師。工人的工資非常低-80 paisa的男性和每天60 paisa的女性。

fact: 1912年3月总督哈丁把驻地迁到德里后，德里民用线（Civil Lines）成为临时首都：该区向北扩展约500英亩，划为通知区，另设五人通知区委员会征收房屋税与水税。高级文官争相租住大宅，该区租金随即暴涨；帝国政府一度想直接收购这些房屋，因印度业主反对而改为承租，政府因此同时成为该区最大的地主与最大的房客，许多业主发现出租比自住更赚钱。

sources.title: A temporary fixture of permanence（Hindustan Times，引 Narayani Gupta《Delhi Between Two Empires》）
sources.quote: With Civil Lines serving as the temporary Capital, civil servants scrambled for big houses, leading to a huge spike in rents in the area. ... The Imperial Government, afraid of the soaring rents, wished to 'acquire' the Civil Lines houses. The Indian owners protested ... the Viceroy decided that the Government would only lease these houses, thus becoming not only the chief landlord (by virtue of the nazul properties), but also the chief tenant in the Civil Lines. Many landowners found it more profitable to lease out their houses than to live in them.

fact: 关于迁都所需土地，英国下议院于1912年2月20日答复：无法在觐见大典宣布之前预购新都用地，宣布之后立即依《印度土地征用法》发出通知，计划在德里城周边强制征收约180平方英里土地。该法允许国家按通知发出之日的市价购买，并给予分割与强制迁离的补偿，但法院在核定补偿时不得计入因迁都而产生的预期增值。

sources.title: India (Removal Of Capital To Delhi)（Hansard，HC Deb 20 February 1912 vol 34 cc432-3）
sources.quote: immediately after the announcement a notification under the Indian Land Acquisition Act was issued, notifying the intention of the Government ... to acquire compulsorily lands to the aggregate amount of about 180 square miles in the vicinity of the present city of Delhi. The Act enables the State to purchase lands so notified at a price based on the market value at the date of the notification, with reasonable compensation for severance and for compulsory dispossession; but in settling the compensation the Courts may not take account of any prospective increase of value.

fact: 大典结束后一周内，内政部即致函旁遮普政府，要求在沙贾汉纳巴德周边划定并公告征地范围，函中明言「德里附近已有人开始炒地，每拖一天价格就更高」。旁遮普方面行动极快：大典结束九天后已公告约11.5万英亩土地，实际上冻结了地价；征地专员比顿估计需向地主发出约8.5万份通知，1912年2月即请求增派助手。

sources.title: From Ghalib's Dilli to Lutyens' New Delhi（Dinyar Patel，导论，引德里档案）
sources.quote: 'It is doubtless within the knowledge of the Government of the Punjab that speculation in land in the neighbourhood of Delhi has already begun,' the department secretary noted, 'and consequently that every day's delay will result in enhanced prices.' ... Observing that some 85,000 notifications would have to be sent out to landowners in the Delhi region, Beadon in February 1912 rather modestly asked the government to provide him with additional assistants. ... nine days after the conclusion of the durbar, Dane had notified property in the Delhi region totalling around 115,000 acres, all but freezing property values.

fact: 1912年初，殖民政府开始征收新都用地，涉及3.5万余英亩、约120个村庄，平均补偿价约为每英亩164卢比；被夺地的业主提起约320起诉讼，四年内全部结案，政府最终只多付了4万卢比。同一材料称，今天新德里同类土地均价约为每英亩1克若尔（1000万卢比）。

sources.title: A Place of One's Own（Tanqeed，引德里土地征收研究）
sources.quote: In early 1912, the colonial government began acquiring over 35,000 acres of land, including 120 villages located in and around the city, through eminent domain. Just four years later, in 1916, the entire process was complete. Land for the new city—which today averages about 1 crore rupees per acre—was acquired by the colonial government for an average of 164 rupees per acre. ... some 320 court cases were filed by dispossessed owners challenging their terms of compensation. Nevertheless, all of these cases were resolved within the same four-year period, resulting in the government having to pay only 40,000 rupees more.

fact: 新德里的实际施工在第一次世界大战之后才大规模展开，1931年完工；为把建材与工人运上拉伊西纳山的岩石山脊，先修了一条环绕议会大厦用地的环形铁路（Imperial Delhi Railway），使用了近二十年。新城于1931年2月10日由总督欧文主持揭幕。

sources.title: New Delhi（Wikipedia，引 New Delhi 建设史）
sources.quote: Construction really began after World War I and was completed by 1931. ... Before construction could begin on the rocky ridge of Raisina Hill, a circular railway line around the Council House (now Parliament House), called the Imperial Delhi Railway, was built to transport construction material and workers for the next twenty years.

fact: 1911年12月大典宣布迁都时，正在卡尔卡—西姆拉铁路段做承包的苏詹·辛格与22岁的索巴·辛格把业务迁到德里，被列为高级承包商。新城的南楼（South Block）与战争纪念拱门（今印度门）由索巴·辛格独家承建，他还承建了总督府部分工程与 Vijay Chowk。

sources.title: Sobha Singh (builder)（Justapedia，转英文维基条目）
sources.quote: When Hardinge, the Viceroy of India, announced the plan to move the British Indian capital city to Delhi ... Sujan Singh and 22-year-old Sobha Singh, who was then a contractor working on the Kalka-Shimla railroad, shifted base to Delhi as building contractors. ... Sujan Singh-Sobha Singh were accepted as senior-grade contractors. ... For the South Block and War Memorial Arch (now India Gate), Sir Sobha was the sole builder.

fact: 索巴·辛格在承建新德里期间大量买地，部分地块的永久保有价低至每平方码2卢比，当时几乎没有其他买主；他随后建成康诺特广场市场群等大量住宅与商业建筑，被称为「半个德里的主人」（adhi dilli ka malik），成为德里最富有的人之一，1944年获封爵士，1978年4月18日去世。

sources.title: Sobha Singh (builder)（Justapedia，转英文维基条目）
sources.quote: Sir Sobha bought as much land in Delhi as he could. He bought several extensive sites at as little as Rs 2 per square yard, freehold. There were few other takers, and he came to be described as adhi dilli ka malik (the owner of half of Delhi). He constructed many residential and commercial buildings, including the Connaught Place market complex ... Sir Sobha Singh was a person of modest education but his success as a builder made him one of the wealthiest persons of Delhi

sources.title: The Man Who Owned 50% of Delhi: The Extraordinary Story of Sobha Singh（News Nest）
sources.quote: When the Delhi Durbar of 1911 heralded the capital's relocation and the decision to build a grand new city designed by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker, Sobha Singh was perfectly positioned ... Instead of spending his earnings lavishly, he invested aggressively in land and rental properties.
